anchor: GS3.1 Indian economy: monetary policy and liquidity management
argumentsAgainst: A one-day operation offers only temporary liquidity absorption and cannot by itself resolve persistent structural liquidity conditions.
Auction participation and the accepted variable rate are not provided in the source, so the realised monetary effect cannot be inferred.
argumentsFor: VRRR gives the RBI a flexible instrument to absorb surplus liquidity for a specified short tenor while retaining the ability to reverse it quickly.
The notified amount, auction window and reversal date make the operation time-bound and operationally transparent.

Unlike a permanent liquidity withdrawal, an overnight VRRR is reversible on the stated date. The precise liquidity impact depends on bids received and accepted; those details are not stated in the source.
indiaImplications: The operation can help align short-term money-market liquidity with the RBI’s monetary-policy stance without changing the policy rate.
Reversal on 6 November 2026 returns the absorbed funds after one day, allowing banks to manage immediate liquidity needs.
The announcement signals active, data-responsive central-bank liquidity management, but the source does not establish the underlying liquidity imbalance or its causes.

officialFacts.text: The RBI decided to conduct a Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction on Thursday, November 05, 2026.
The notified amount for the auction was ₹75,000 crore.
The auction window was 09:30 AM to 10:00 AM.
The date of reversal was November 06, 2026 (Friday).
The operational guidelines for the auction as given in the Reserve Bank’s Press Release 2019-2020/1947 dated February 13, 2020 will remain the same.

example.text: If banks place funds with the RBI in the announced one-day auction, those funds would be absorbed temporarily and scheduled for reversal the next day. This is an illustration of the stated tenor and reversal design, not a claim about actual bids or participation.

question.answer: The operation can absorb short-term liquidity without permanently withdrawing funds: banks place funds through the auction, and the RBI reverses the transaction after one day. Because the source does not report bids or accepted rates, its realised impact cannot be quantified.

sections.heading: RBI schedules temporary liquidity absorption
paragraphs: The Reserve Bank of India announced on 4 November 2026 that it would conduct a ₹75,000 crore VRRR auction on 5 November for one day. The auction window was 9:30 AM–10:00 AM, with reversal scheduled for 6 November. [P1]

sections.heading: Mechanism and limitation
paragraphs: A VRRR auction can temporarily absorb funds from participating banks through a variable, auction-determined rate. The stated reversal date limits the operation’s duration. However, the announcement does not disclose bids, accepted amounts or the accepted rate, so it cannot establish the operation’s realised market impact. The RBI also said that the operational guidelines from its 13 February 2020 press release would remain unchanged. [P1]

staticDefinition: A Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility is an auction-based instrument through which the RBI can temporarily absorb liquidity from participating institutions at a rate discovered through bidding, subject to the applicable operational guidelines.
use: Use the announcement to illustrate calibrated, reversible liquidity management in answers on monetary policy, money markets and the RBI’s operational framework.

advisory_notes: The claim that VRRR uses an auction-determined rate is consistent with the instrument’s framework, but the supplied announcement itself does not state the rate-discovery mechanics.
“Without changing the policy rate” is a reasonable analytical inference, not a fact established by this announcement alone.
“Returns the absorbed funds” should be framed as scheduled reversal; actual funds and amount depend on bids accepted and settlement.
The phrase “banks place funds” is a general mechanism explanation; specify eligible participants rather than implying every bank participates.
“Align short-term money-market liquidity with the monetary-policy stance” is analytical framing and should not be presented as the announcement’s stated purpose.
The headline and deck accurately reproduce the announcement’s one-day tenor, amount, window and reversal date.
The hypothetical example is correctly labelled and does not assert actual participation or realised absorption.
GS3 monetary policy and liquidity management is a valid UPSC connection; GS3.2 may be overly broad unless that code specifically covers the relevant syllabus segment.

wayForward: Use short-term liquidity operations in conjunction with clear communication of the monetary-policy stance.
Assess the realised effect through auction participation, accepted amounts, rates and subsequent money-market conditions; these are not available in the source.
Maintain transparency about the duration, notified amount, auction window and reversal date.
